tax.title: Sebaetdon and gift tax
items: Gifts such as sebaetdon that are considered customary under social norms are not subject to gift tax (Inheritance and Gift Tax Act Art. 46, Enforcement Decree Art. 35).

If the money is saved in deposits or invested in stocks under the child's name, it is hard to treat as a tax-free gift and may count as a taxable gift. The National Tax Service says money received for living or education costs is not tax-free once it goes into savings or stock purchases.

A minor can receive up to ₩20 million over 10 years from parents or grandparents tax-free (gift deduction). Adults get ₩50 million, and gifts from other relatives such as aunts and uncles get ₩10 million over 10 years (Art. 53).
If you plan to keep saving in the child's name, filing a gift tax return even within the deduction makes it easier to explain where the money came from later.

exchange.title: Getting new bills
items: Before Seollal and Chuseok, the Bank of Korea sets a period for exchanging new bills at its head office and regional branches. The 2027 Seollal schedule has not been announced yet, so the notes below follow previous years.
For Seollal 2026, the head office (Namdaemun, Seoul) exchanged bills on Feb 4–13 and the 16 regional branches on Feb 9–13, cash only.
The Bank of Korea head office's holiday limit per person per day is ₩1 million each in ₩50,000 and ₩10,000 bills, ₩500,000 in ₩5,000 bills and ₩200,000 in ₩1,000 bills. Regional branches may differ.
Ask your local bank branch ahead of time too. New bills run out quickly right before the holiday.

tips.title: Envelope tips
items: You need one envelope per person. Writing names or relations on them in advance avoids mix-ups.
Bill counts use the fewest bills, largest first. If young children would rather get several ₩10,000 bills, prepare five ₩10,000 bills instead of one ₩50,000 bill.
Agreeing on amounts per age group with your siblings avoids hurt feelings when kids compare.
Your list is saved on this device, and a share link shows the same list to family.

origin.title: Where sebaetdon comes from
items: Elders giving New Year wishes after a bow is an old custom, but the first record of money is said to be in Haedong Jukji (1925), which mentions giving 'sebaetgap' when a child bows.
Money in envelopes is seen in China from the 11th century and in Japan from the 17th century, and one view is that the custom came in after Korea's ports opened.
In harder times, families likely gave new clothes or food instead of money (National Folk Museum researcher, Seoul Shinmun, 2019).

items.q: How much sebaetdon is right for Seollal 2027?
items.a: There is no fixed rule. Press reports around Seollal 2026 put it at about ₩10–30k for preschool and lower elementary, ₩30–50k for upper elementary, ₩50–100k for middle and high school, and ₩100–200k for college students and job seekers. This calculator fills in the most commonly mentioned amount within each range.

items.q: For middle and high schoolers, is ₩50,000 or ₩100,000 more common?
items.a: KakaoPay money-envelope data show ₩100,000 was the most common amount at Seollal 2025 (42%). At Seollal 2024, ₩50,000 (39%) was slightly ahead of ₩100,000 (37%), with an average of ₩74,000.

items.q: How much do people give their parents?
items.a: KakaoPay money envelopes to parents averaged about ₩200,000 at Seollal 2024 and ₩227,000 at Seollal 2025. In a 2023 Hanwha Life staff survey, ₩300,000 (36.2%) and ₩200,000 (26.6%) were the most common answers.

items.q: When and where can I get new bills?
items.a: The Bank of Korea runs a new-bill exchange period at its head office and regional branches one to two weeks before Seollal. In 2026 it was Feb 4–13 at the head office and Feb 9–13 at regional branches, cash only. Check the Bank of Korea notice for 2027.

items.q: Is sebaetdon subject to gift tax?
items.a: Customary sebaetdon is not taxed. But if it is saved or invested in the child's account, it may be treated as a gift. Keep in mind that a minor can receive up to ₩20 million over 10 years from parents or grandparents within the deduction.

items.q: How are the bills for each envelope worked out?
items.a: Each amount is split into the fewest bills starting from ₩50,000. For example, ₩78,000 is one ₩50,000, two ₩10,000, one ₩5,000 and three ₩1,000 bills. The totals across the list are the new bills to prepare.
